# Commits exempted from the no-commit-trailers gate — a RATCHET, not an allowlist.
#
# Entries may only be REMOVED, never added -- with ONE narrow exception, stated
# here so it cannot be read as general permission (#17717).
#
# A new commit carrying a banned trailer must be fixed BEFORE it lands, not
# recorded here. The gate has no mechanism to add to this file, and adding one
# would defeat the rule.
#
# THE EXCEPTION: a trailer that no branch commit carried, stamped onto the
# squash result by GitHub's merge from a misconfigured local author identity,
# and discovered only when a promotion PR first scans the landed range. Such a
# commit could not have been fixed before it landed -- the trailer did not exist
# until the merge -- and `main` cannot be rewritten to strip it. Nothing else
# qualifies. In particular a trailer that WAS present on a branch commit does
# not: that one was fixable, and the fix is to fix it.
#
# WHAT THE ENTRY COUNT IS NOT (#15897)
#
# This file's line count is not a census of banned-trailer commits in this
# repository's history. The gate that reads it is scoped to `pull_request`,
# comparing `BASE..HEAD` — it examines only the commits a PR introduces, by
# design, never the branch's full history. Applying the same predicate this
# gate uses (anchored, case-insensitive, owner/bot exemptions applied) to
# every commit on `main` finds roughly 7,000 more matches than this file has
# entries, almost all of them predating this policy — legitimately out of
# scope, not a backlog. Rewriting that history to strip them means force-
# pushing a shared branch out from under every worktree and session based on
# it, which the project's own rules forbid for a cosmetic correction. See
# docs/developer/RATCHET_BASELINES.md for the full measurement and reasoning.
#
# WHY THESE FOUR EXIST
#
# The repository's `.git/config` on the maintainer's workstation carried a local
# override of `user.name = test` / `user.email = test@test`, shadowing the
# correct global identity (`mrveiss` / martins.veiss@gmail.com). Branch commits
# were therefore authored as `test <test@test>`, and GitHub's squash-merge
# stamped that identity onto the resulting commit as a `Co-authored-by:` trailer.
#
# The gate correctly rejected them: a `Co-authored-by:` naming neither the
# commit's own author, nor the owner, nor a bot reads as a genuine third-party
# human co-author, which is exactly what the rule exists to prevent
# (`no-commit-trailers.yml`, #13654).
#
# The trailers are not real attribution. `test <test@test>` is not a person; it
# is a misconfigured identity, since corrected by unsetting the local override so
# the global one applies. Nothing is being concealed by exempting them.
#
# WHY NOT REWRITE THEM
#
# Stripping the trailers means rewriting history from the earliest offender
# (26 commits) and force-pushing `main`. Roughly 32 worktrees and several
# concurrent sessions are based on that branch; every one would need re-basing,
# and the project's own rules forbid force-pushing a shared branch. That is a
# real operational risk traded for a cosmetic correction.
#
# These surfaced only when a release PR first scanned the whole `release..main`
# range; per-PR scans never saw them, because the trailer was added BY the squash
# merge rather than being present on the branch.
#
# One SHA per line. Everything after `#` is a comment.

# #16268: ONE-TIME ADDITION by owner decision (11 Sep 2026), against the rule at
# the top of this file.
#
# These eighteen owner-authored squash commits, 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-10, carry a
# `Co-authored-by: t <...>` trailer naming neither the owner, a bot, nor the
# commit's own author. They sit in `release..main`, so the first release-sync
# PR (#16246) could never pass `No commit trailers`. The owner chose to baseline
# exactly these commits as full SHAs, and nothing else: the check stays strict
# for every other commit. The list is the output of
#   git log --format=%H -i --grep='^co-authored-by: *t <' origin/release..origin/main
# which returned exactly these eighteen when they were recorded.

# #17717: SECOND-INSTANCE ADDITION by owner decision (28 Sep 2026), under the
# narrow exception stated at the top of this file.
#
# A DIFFERENT CAUSE FROM THE `test <test@test>` BATCH ABOVE. Do not read the two
# as one recurrence, and do not diagnose this one by checking git config -- that
# was tried first and it comes back clean, because there is no override to find.
#
# `t <t@example.invalid>` is this repository's TEST-FIXTURE git identity. Ten
# files carry it; eight run `git commit` while exercising hooks, branch guards
# or changed-file logic, and two of those are in `repo_tests/` and so run under
# the pre-push hook. A test that commits with `-c user.name=t` while an ambient
# `GIT_DIR` points at the real repository creates a real commit authored `t` on
# the real branch -- #15353, test suites writing commits onto the working repo.
# GitHub's squash then collects every branch commit's author as a
# `Co-authored-by:` on the merged result, which is the only place the identity
# survives: NO commit on `main` is AUTHORED by `t`, checked.
#
# So per-PR scans pass -- including #17696's own -- because the gate compares
# BASE..HEAD and the trailer does not exist until the merge creates it. Only a
# promotion re-scans the landed range.
#
# WHY IT REACHES THE REAL REPOSITORY AT ALL: an inherited `GIT_DIR` OUTRANKS
# `-C <path>` and `cwd=`. A git hook exports it, so under the pre-push hook a
# test's `git init` in a temp directory re-initialises the repository that
# variable names instead -- `repo_tests/hooks_path_override_15961_test.py:450`
# records learning this the hard way.
#
# THREE OF THE FIXTURE FILES MAKE IT WORSE THAN A PER-BRANCH LEAK. They write
# the identity with `git config` rather than passing `-c` per invocation
# (`scripts/lib/branch-guards_test.sh:117`,
# `scripts/lib/session-handoffs_test.sh:88`,
# `repo_tests/hooks_path_override_15961_test.py:479`). Worktrees share ONE
# config through the common dir, so a single unscrubbed config write sets the
# identity for every worktree at once -- which is the shape of five commits
# across five branches in one afternoon.
#
# WHAT BOUNDS IT, HONESTLY. Every one of those sites currently scrubs: all eight
# committing tests pass `scrubbed_git_env()` (`autobot_shared/paths.py`), and
# all three config writers unset the ambient variables. Verified per file, not
# assumed from the helper's existence. So NO CURRENT TEST LEAKS.
#
# The open window is a NEW test that commits or writes config, run before its
# scrub is added -- which is exactly what happened here: 969c1956 is the commit
# that introduced one such test. So the class recurs per newly-written fixture
# rather than per branch, it can hit every worktree from one run, and it closes
# when #15353 does. #16124 is the detection gap. #16268 is the release-facing
# home carrying 18 of these from an earlier promotion; these five are recorded
# there too.
#
# `t <t@example.invalid>` is not a person and claims no attribution.
#
# CLASS 2 -- FOUR SHAS, A DIFFERENT AND WORSE CAUSE. Exempted by explicit owner
# ruling (28 Sep 2026) and NOT A PRECEDENT. Read this before citing this file.
#
# `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` is a REAL ATTRIBUTION CLAIM.
# It is the exact thing `no-commit-trailers.yml` (#13654) exists to reject --
# not a fixture artefact, not a misconfigured identity -- so none of the
# reasoning above reaches it and the narrow exception at the top of this file
# does not cover it. These four are exempted for ONE reason: they are already on
# `main` and rewriting a shared branch to strip them is forbidden. History is
# immutable; that is the entire justification. The trailer is not acceptable.
#
# A FUTURE COMMIT CARRYING IT MUST BE FIXED BEFORE IT LANDS, AND THIS FILE IS
# NOT WHERE IT GOES.
#
# Its source is open, which makes it worse than class 1 rather than merely
# different: the agent harness instructs each session to append that trailer,
# while this project forbids commit trailers entirely and this gate enforces the
# project. A session obeying its harness and one obeying the project are both
# doing as told, so instances keep landing until that is resolved at the source
# (#17719). Class 1 is bounded by a scrub that already exists; class 2 is
# bounded by nothing yet.
